#142959. WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1470 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

WoW: Forever Wants To Get Rid Of The Idea Of “BiS” Gear

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1470 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices.
  • In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's upcoming items, class changes, and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is approaching itemization and "best-in-slot" (BiS) gear differently, with developer Blizzard instead wanting players to have more boss- or biome-specific choices. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard dove deep on the MMORPG's itemization changes, how it approached designing Forever's fresh items, class changes, and more. On the subject of raid gear and chase items, Forever senior game designer Aidan Moon mentioned something that could be seen as controversial in certain circles of the game's community. "I essentially want to get rid of BiS," Moon said. "I think that BiS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about [the] role-playing aspects of it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=67dDe3QgJtM BiS is WoW shorthand for essentially the best item that could possibly be in a given gear slot for a specific class. Look up any WoW guide for WoW Classic or modern WoW, and you'll find class BiS gear lists telling players exactly what they should be wearing in order for their character to be as powerful as possible. Endgame in many ways revolves around acquiring your BiS gear, first your "pre-raid" BiS from gear available in max-level dungeons, and then BiS gear, like tier sets, from raids. It's for that exact reason Forever introduced new items that grant additional stats or effects against certain enemy types or even in certain locations. Moon gave an example of specific items that deal more damage against Murloc enemies, and that players might want to have more gear tailored to fighting against a Murloc boss in a raid encounter. Forever's raids will feature multiple distinct biomes within them, Moon revealed, giving players more factors to consider when choosing what gear to use for specific parts of each raid. One wing of a raid may be snowy, while another may be cavernous, changing what gear could be more optimal for those encounters. "I think your BiS should be different [for] every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," Moon said. "It should be based on the creature and the biome and a mixture of those two. You might have an item that's really good against snowy, and then another item in that same slot that's really good against Murlocs. Then there's a Murloc boss in a snowy area and you're just like 'Which one do I wear?' And then eventually you get to a point where you're swapping those things out or it's too much cognitive load and you don't want to do that. It's for those players that really want to optimize."  Trying to get rid of BiS lists is a significant change for WoW, which has revolved around the idea for over two decades. Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones. "I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon said. Of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt swiftly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse. Blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier. It's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. Blizzard recently lifted the veil on how Forever's new PvP system will work, revealing how classic WoW's infamous rank grind will now be a thing of the past.

Players can already encounter some of the itemization ideas Moon discussed while leveling to 60, with low-level gear from dungeons and quests dealing more damage against specified enemy types or even granting additional movement speed in specific zones.

"I don't want you to have to ever think about BiS, I just want you to think about the fight right in front of you and how you're going to fight it," Moon noted.

It has been revealed that of course, having more biome- or enemy-type-specific items means hoarding more pieces of gear as opposed to selling old ones when an upgrade comes around. That will no doubt swiftly fill up the inventories and banks of players looking to min-max for every possible scenario. Classic WoW is already notorious for having limited bag space, and players running around with multiple sets of hyper-specific gear will only make that pain point worse.

Sources indicate that blizzard sounds like it's aware of that problem. Principal game designer Kris Zierhut said bigger bags are on that way, but that it's not needed right now immediately post-launch. However, Blizzard knows players will eventually need more bag space as well as better ways to organize and search for owned items to make putting together encounter-specific sets of gear easier.

According to recent reports, it's a massive change, but the strategy Blizzard is employing seems to be working. Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent and weekly player records, and more than 15 million characters have been created in the MMO so far. Blizzard recently lifted the veil on how Forever's fresh PvP system will work, revealing how classic WoW's infamous rank grind will now be a thing of the past.

When MacPaw debuted Moonlock on the Mac, the organization described its newly introduced app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Users can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the tech giant states “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping customers improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets consumers rapidly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

Recent findings suggest that as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, consumers can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

Recent findings suggest that “When we launched Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

It has been revealed that for William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

Right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

Industry observers note that for Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a new step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an important role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

Russell Brand’s wife, Laura Brand, stated she will “honor” the rules of his prison after controversy over a message she read out from the incarcerated comedian declaring his innocence.

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer confirmed last week that Brand’s message — read out by Laura on the November 15 episode of their “Sunday Service” podcast — was being investigated to determine whether it had violated U.K. laws that ban prisoners from making statements that may cause distress to victims.

“Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention, and now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey [in Cambridgeshire, England], I will absolutely honor that,” Laura, 39, said at the beginning of the latest episode of the “Sunday Service” podcast on Sunday, November 22.

Just days after Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10 and a half years behind bars for rape and sexual assault, the disgraced star declared his innocence in a missive read by his wife on their YouTube podcast.

“Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,” Brand declared in the message.

It has been revealed that “This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules,” a spokesperson for Starmer mentioned in a statement on November 16.

“Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances,” the spokesperson added. “Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments.”.

On the latest episode of her podcast, Laura explained why she is continuing forward with “Sunday Service,” which she once cohosted with her husband.

Industry observers note that “I’m choosing to continue ‘Sunday Service’ because I really enjoy it,” she mentioned. “It continues to be a great education for me, and I enjoy reading the supportive comments, and I am so heartened by the many of the messages that I got, and that is what inspired me to do it this week and look at the ways I can continue to and move forward with this.”.

Industry News: Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let customers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Industry observers note that google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for users whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Industry observers note that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let customers run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let customers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the company discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with new scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Industry observers note that google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for users whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a new service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Industry observers note that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let customers run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google launched the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One customers, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Sources indicate that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

It’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

But perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that users want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the firm hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

It has been revealed that many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

Recent findings suggest that there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

Recent findings suggest that if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

60 hours in GTA 6 has me yearning for an online Leonida

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida.
  • Sources indicate that pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction.
  • It has been revealed that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida. Rockstar has delivered on its promise of both breadth and depth—the map is huge, but utterly stuffed with detail. Large, open highways shrink into single lanes surrounded by construction that force me to slam the brakes. Sidewalks sparse with pedestrians eventually lead to densely packed retail areas, restaurants, and clubs.

Sources indicate that pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction. You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.

It has been revealed that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting. I spent an ungodly amount of time in GTA 5's Online mode when it first released. I was there on the ground for its incredibly shaky launch (I made a character and then got stuck in that birdseye view loading screen for hours, incredible stuff) and continued to sink time into it over the years, particularly during Covid.

It has been revealed that and I like it well enough, but its novelty has waned over the last decade. Its core experience is inherently different from what singleplayer brings, and I had yearned to return to a world less about blowing other players up with flying motorbikes and more about, well, blowing non-players up with regular motorbikes.

But after 60 hours roaming around Leonida and witnessing what it has to offer? I now want nothing more than for Rockstar to spin this map into the next generation of Online. Even outside of missions and driving around, there are so many little things that I would kill to do with pals.

Sources indicate that grab a pack of brewskis from the convenience store, hop in a boat, and go fishing. Throw on our best all-American attire and get down and dirty in some mud racing. Seek out other players meticulously planning a jewellery store hold-up, only to swoop in and steal the goods for ourselves. Hit up the gym for a little workout before nipping to a nearby restaurant for a bite to eat. Leonida is a place that is so rife with things to do, and I can imagine doing almost all of them with some buddies by my side.

It's also the perfect opportunity for Rockstar to introduce things that are sorely missing for me right now. A lack of safehouses makes sense with GTA 6's offline story, but I yearn to buy highrise apartments and suburban houses. Maybe even buy a business or two, for a little side cash. There's also the matter of that gigantic casino and the go-kart track that are currently inaccessible but the latter of which is donning a large "COMING SOON" sign. It feels like I'm being taunted. Surely you wouldn't put these things in the game with no intention of opening them at some point… right?

According to recent reports, and even as someone who was never interested in nor dabbled with GTA Online's flourishing roleplaying scene, I've encountered so many instances where I've thought roleplaying in Leonida actually be pretty darn neat. I could become a RydeMe driver, or a Snapmatic influencer, or a backwater recluse who lives off the land. And when the game comes to PC? The potential for bending the world to account for even more professions becomes all the greater.

In a recent development, rockstar hasn't actually remarked a damn thing about GTA 6 Online right now, but it feels inevitable. Leonida is the biggest playground the developer has given players to date, and unleashing players across its sprawling map is Online's natural evolution. And, y'know, considering how much money GTAO has made over the last 13 years, I'm almost certain that Rockstar won't leave that kind of opportunity on the table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem. Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on. The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the company sees it as a cheeky little homage. But the controllers for the console? They look terrible: Eww. In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are noted to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars, I have to give the movie its flowers.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This year’s Christmas movie releases are in full swing now that it’s mid-November, and I knew I had to check out Guarding Stars with my Netflix subscription. I mean, it unites Gilmore Girls’ Jared Padalecki with Gossip Girl’s Leighton Meester, so I was in for the 2000s nostalgia alone. I was really digging this lighthearted rom-com (that’s sometimes an action movie), but then that twist just made me go “WTF!” Let’s talk about it. But be warned, there are SPOILERS ahead!

Before we get into my lows about Guarding Stars, I have to give the movie its flowers. I’ve seen a lot of holiday rom-coms, and this one had the right amount of sweetness and depth I want from this kind of movie. It follows the fake dating trope pretty much to a T, but I really enjoyed what Padalecki and Meester in particular brought to it as Jack and Hannah.

Recent findings suggest that it’s the kind of movie where we all know they were going to fall in love by the end, but I was instantly curious about how these two were going to fall for each other. I like that they brought out the softness in each other despite both of them being otherwise hardened by their current lives, and I really liked the mother/son dynamic between Jack and Andie Macdowell’s Connie.

In a recent development, guarding Stars also had that nice balance of goofiness, wit and emotion that I want to see from a Christmas Netflix movie that stopped it from falling into simply being a holiday screensaver. I know it’s based on a popular book called The Bodyguard, and after seeing it I would definitely pick it up, especially to see what changes were made.

However, I thought the Guarding Stars really dropped the ball on the whole “stalker” plotline. Not that I’d expect it to be a huge part of the movie to begin with, but when it was revealed that Nadine was Jack’s stalker near the end, I was so taken aback. It felt way too convenient that one of two people he meets outside of his family and his bodyguard crew ended up being the stalker, and particularly having happened to be in the same place where he was hiding away.

To me, it would have made a lot more sense if the stalker travelled to his location after seeing the kiss cam video with Hannah go viral. Instead, the only information we get is that they knew each other in high school and she divorced her husband to be with him. And then, her husband was somehow vengeful of Jack? The stalker payoff was so unbelievably thin, and felt like a bummer. Especially when the rest of the rom-com put a lot of attention on character development and fun moments for the other characters.

It has been revealed that perhaps the filmmaking team thought the audience wouldn’t care about the plotline not concerning the romance? But, to me, it just cheapened the rest of the viewing experience. I hope more Netflix rom-coms can build out their scripts. If it’s going to be partly an action mystery, I don’t want to feel like no attention was put on that aspect of the movie.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that look, all in all, Guarding Stars had some elements that had me putting it on the nice and naughty list, but overall, I’m happy I checked it out. But come on, Netflix, if you want to shock me, I know you can do better than that.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap. "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them. This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were swiftly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme. While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to concern a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent manufacturer, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

In a recent development, google launched Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

To me, this is the most useful new feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each initiative includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

Recent findings suggest that when it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is at the moment open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

Plans can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

It has been revealed that ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google notes this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

Industry observers note that if you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

Industry observers note that these updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

A spokesperson for his office told The Independent, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." Rockstar North is based in Edinburgh, Scotland, but GTA 6 was made by thousands of people across the globe. GTA is also historically linked to the UK, as the original game, 1997's Grand Theft Auto, was made by DMA Design in Edinburgh. Asked if the PM himself would play GTA 6, his office said Burnham is too busy right now. "He won't be playing it," the spokesperson said. GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the fresh version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

Joseph Zada has had a lot to say about the process it took to become Haymitch in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, so I wasn’t surprised he had more to say. However, the actor “being completely honest” about something he didn’t like wasn’t on my Bingo card… and this time it’s not about how Zada’s hair is different. The actor shared his hot take about Sunrise on the Reaping making him say ‘Lenore Dove’ over and over, and I have to admit, he has a point.

The actor brought the energy while discussing the movie during a BBC Radio 1 interview, and two of his co-stars had to step in to lend a helping (and humorous) hand. When it came to saying his girlfriend’s name, he didn’t understand why he had to say the full thing:.

I did not want to say 'Lenore Dove.' Didn’t want to say the full name. Didn’t want to say the full name! What are you talking about? Actually, I shouldn’t go that far. But like it’s your girlfriend! That’s why I went to darling a lot. But like you have to say the full–there’s not many people you have to say their full name the whole time.

While Zada explained, Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove, first chose to stay out of it, saying, “I’m so quiet right now.” Something tells me she’s heard this hot take a few times while filming. The actor shared that he attempted to sneak in a “Lenore,” but director Francis Lawrence wasn’t having it and would correct him. Zada assumes the precise name was a Suzanne Collins choice, which is the second time Peak playfully intervenes by shushing him.

His energy would make fans proud, as I’ve seen plenty of hot takes regarding the book-to-screen adaptations. Those were mostly back in the Peeta vs. Gale days. Thankfully, Zada's other co-star, Mckenna Grace, sweeps in at the last second to clarify his comments:.

I think that the point, before you get yourself in trouble, is that Joe is trying to make, as his media-trained translator, I think that you’re trying to say that because ya’ll have such a close bond, you didn’t wanna feel like you were calling her her full government name the whole time.

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that VWFNDR + MBL introduced on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial revision.

It has been revealed that on Android, this comes in the form of newly introduced color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

Industry observers note that in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

In a recent development, consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Upcoming Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

In a recent development, so we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

It has been revealed that but why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

In a recent development, let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in Newly introduced York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a massive turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

In a recent development, at the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” indicates Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”.

Recent findings suggest that today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”.

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” states Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”.

According to recent reports, it certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”.

According to recent reports, bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

According to recent reports, dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

For actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” says Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”.

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

Industry observers note that hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup this year has been one of the best yet. From reinventing the time-loop wheel to an incredible third season of Mistletoe Murders, it’s been hit after hit, and it doesn't seem to be slowing down. In fact, Thanksgiving week is going to be even bigger with the release of Lacey Chabert’s Disney World movie and Rachael Leigh Cook’s newest film, where she pulls double duty playing twins. I'm excited to see Cook take on the roles, but I'm also surprised over a concern she had.

Acting in general is hard, but having to act opposite yourself while playing co-leads of a movie is even harder (unless you're Lindsey Lohan, who found playing twins easy). Cook is obviously a veteran at this point, so I never would've expected that she would feel apprehensive every time she stepped on set of Double Booked for the Holidays:.

Industry observers note that I was concerned that there wouldn’t be enough conflict within the movie because I was too far inside it. I was concerned that just me yapping away at myself was going to be a bad time.

The She’s All That star is set to play identical twins Abigail and Charlie, who end up in Wales for Christmas to help run an AirBnb/bookshop for the week. While there, both women connect with local men: Tom (Owain Yeoman), a barista who works next to the shop, and Lord Rhys (Stephan Hagan), the son of the author behind a popular book series that takes place in the town.

Sources indicate that cook might be concerned about the lack of conflict within the narrative, but I don’t think she has anything to fret about. After all, neither Tom nor Lord Rhys are aware that Abigail and Charlie are twins, which is bound to lead to some hilarious and maybe even tense situations.

Still, the actress couldn’t help but worry when she realized how much screen time she’d be sharing with herself, telling Us Weekly:.

When I started to watch it, my first reaction to seeing myself in stereo was, ‘Oh no, this is way too much. I’m the worst scene partner I’ve ever had. This was a bad idea.’ Because it’s a lot. But then I was able to sort of relax into it and say, ‘OK, I think I was able to differentiate them by enough.’.

Differentiating between Abigail and Charlie brought up its own set of complications for Cook, as her characters are identical twins with similar preferences when it comes to their appearance. This is definitely something that hasn’t been done before, since most movies that feature twins give each character something unique to help audiences tell the difference. Thankfully, Cook found other ways to help audiences tell her characters apart — at least she hopes she did:.

I knew that the worst thing people could feel while watching was confusion. So that was high on my priority list to avoid.

In a recent development, hallmark movies aren’t known for their confusing nature, so I’m feeling confident about the direction of the film. If anything, it might feel like an immersive experience if viewers can’t tell her characters apart and could allow them to empathize with the men who are falling for Cook's respective characters.

Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon. Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a new GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world." Zelnick, for his part, remarked people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7. "I can't help myself. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously. For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first.

It has been revealed that leaker Ice Universe notes Apple is at the moment developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20. We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical new design with an all-glass appearance.

Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product ….

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

Ice Universe states that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.

Apple is right now developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of fresh devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

We’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report says the bezels are around 1mm thick.

The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

We yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's quickly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

In a recent development, this earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her upcoming direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very rapidly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

Michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she states more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

Certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to Latest Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

Recent findings suggest that according to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a upcoming blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”.

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, claims Myers.

Sources indicate that “William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers claims.

Sources indicate that according to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

“I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers says. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to New Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”.

According to recent reports, the visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.).

Sources indicate that william and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

It has been revealed that “The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower notes.

According to recent reports, “William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader intends. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental concerns and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, shows his pulling power and influence.”.

  • In a recent development, these days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times.
  • Recent findings suggest that caesar asks Peeta how his 'latest leg' is working out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I’ll never forget when I went to see one of my favorite novels at the time become a book-to-screen adaptation back in 2012. I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

In a recent development, these days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games. Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:.

Recent findings suggest that caesar asks Peeta how his 'latest leg' is working out. 'New leg?' I say, and I can't help reaching out and pulling up the bottom of Peeta's pants. 'Oh, no,' I whisper,' taking in the metal-and-plastic device that has replaced his flesh.

According to recent reports, in the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

I think when The Hunger Games movie came out, I thought the movie was censoring an important aspect of the story. Peeta’s major injury really had me on the edge of my seat while I was reading the book, so it was sort of anticlimactic for the movie to completely skip it.

However, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

Recent findings suggest that there’s something else. Ultimately, I’m realizing that both Peeta and Katniss have so many horrific things happen to them throughout the series that maybe it was OK for the movies to skip Peeta losing a leg. I mean, what happens to Peeta in Mockingjay alone is just heartbreaking. The guy loses his entire family, he’s captured by the Capitol and starved. And then, his brain is altered so he thinks Katniss is his enemy. That’s some really rough stuff.

Now, I think overall The Hunger Games movie series did a great job of adapting the maturity of the book series, but now I’m OK with the films taking out a few extra traumatic things like Peeta’s amputated leg.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some significant numbers that speak to the pent-up demand.
  • It has been revealed that for starters, the internet service provider Comcast declared that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the manufacturer's history in terms of demand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release. For starters, the internet service provider Comcast confirmed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the organization's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast mentioned around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the Fresh Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said. A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight. Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster. Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox. These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

It has been revealed that rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some significant numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release.

It has been revealed that for starters, the internet service provider Comcast declared that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the manufacturer's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network.

GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast stated around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the Newly introduced Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said.

A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight.

Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster.

Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox.

Industry observers note that these daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella stated. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said.

It has been revealed that for more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

You Can Try WhatsApp's Latest Disappearing Text Messages Early

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • According to recent reports, that's now changing.
  • As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

According to recent reports, that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an vital account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a latest "View Once" option as well.

As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

As mentioned above, this feature is right now in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That mentioned, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

If you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest upgrade. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

#142922. This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2179 w)
