Kirby fans have had plenty on their plate lately, and it seems Nintendo is going to keep the good times rolling. Last year brought a latest entry in the Kirby Air Riders series, along with a beefy expansion to Kirby and the Forgotten Land for the Switch 2 titled Star-Crossed World. Next up is Kirby and the World Beyond, a new open-ended 3D entry in the series that looks to pick up where Forgotten Land left off. The game is slated for early 2027.

The latest matter of Nintendo’s catalog highlights many of the game’s upcoming features. While many of these details were revealed previously or hinted at in the game’s reveal trailer, the article offers more specifics.

Recent findings suggest that as translated by Genki_JPN on X, the fresh game will let Kirby travel in an open-world environment using abilities copied from enemies. For instance, you can ride the blade from the classic Cutter power-up to quickly cross terrain. Kirby can also use the Bomb ability to make big vertical leaps and the Parasol to glide through the air. The article emphasizes that the game will have an expansive setting, suggesting it will be fully open-world and let players explore at their own pace.

A “mysterious girl” who was previously kidnapped by King Dedede will play an important role in the story. She’s purple with white hair and, in a rare move for this series, is humanoid rather than shaped like an orb. The article once again draws attention to how, after Kirby sends DeeDee flying, he leaves a “hole in the sky,” suggesting that Kirby is trapped in some sort of The Truman Show-like enclosure.

Recent findings suggest that “What awaits Kirby beyond the other side of the massive wall he destroyed with his newfound powers?” the article asks. This imagery invites many questions: Was Kirby abducted and transferred into this enclosure at some point, or has he always lived in this “fake” world? How does this tie in with the post-apocalyptic reveals from Kirby and the Forgotten Land, if at all?

Recent findings suggest that despite its cutesy aesthetic, the Kirby series has always been willing to go to unexpected places. By the end of a given adventure, this pink orb is usually battling interdimensional beings beyond human understanding with names like "Nightmare" and "Dark Nebula." World Beyond seems to be getting existential in a different way, taking things in a fourth-wall-breaking direction. We'll see how this all pans out next year when the game releases in Spring 2027.

Curry Barker Would Have Completely Reshot ‘Obsession’ If He Could

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been quite a year for Curry Barker.
  • Which is why it’s interesting that Hollywood’s hottest new director took time out from editing (he’s cutting “Ghosts” himself) and writing (“I have my next thing that I’m working on — I’m really excited about it, and nobody knows anything about it, which is super exciting”), and an unexpected Oscar campaign (“Obsession” is a legit contender for Best Picture, Actress, and Original Screenplay nominations), to make a 5-minute short film, “Mama Bear.” On this week’s episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Barker talked about how the success of “Obsession” interrupted his established flow of churning out short-form content for his popular YouTube channel.
  • “I have two or three short films where I’m like, ‘Oh man, this all took off really promptly, and I have this short film idea I’ve been dying to do,” noted Barker on Toolkit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been quite a year for Curry Barker. In September 2025, he brought his $700,000 horror film to the Toronto International Film Festival, where it sparked a bidding war that Focus Features won for $17 million. That hefty price tag turned into the deal of the century, as “Obsession” went on to become a half-billion-dollar box-office sensation, with audiences growing week to week. It was clear the then 26-year-old “YouTuber” (a moniker Barker rightfully dismisses) was something special. This was not just a flash in the pan, but a real talent with a seemingly boundless number of ideas and movies he wanted to make. His next film, “Anything but Ghosts,” was already in the can by the “Obsession” premiere, a yet-to-be-confirmed third film is in the works, while potential franchises (“Texas Chainsaw Massacre” and “Obsession,” Barker sees the One Wish Willow story device having “Knives Out” anthology-like potential) linger in the background. Related Stories Director Brian Duffield Had to Find a Latest Form of Visual Storytelling for ‘Whalefall’ How ‘Paper Tiger’ Evolved When Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway Couldn’t Reprise Their ‘Armageddon Time’ Roles.

Which is why it’s interesting that Hollywood’s hottest new director took time out from editing (he’s cutting “Ghosts” himself) and writing (“I have my next thing that I’m working on — I’m really excited about it, and nobody knows anything about it, which is super exciting”), and an unexpected Oscar campaign (“Obsession” is a legit contender for Best Picture, Actress, and Original Screenplay nominations), to make a 5-minute short film, “Mama Bear.” On this week’s episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Barker talked about how the success of “Obsession” interrupted his established flow of churning out short-form content for his popular YouTube channel.

“I have two or three short films where I’m like, ‘Oh man, this all took off really promptly, and I have this short film idea I’ve been dying to do,” noted Barker on Toolkit. “I actually have no time to do those short films, and then justifying if it be would be worth my time to do them when I need to be writing this, I need to be editing this, and I need to be doing press for this.”.

It’s less about Barker’s desire to scratch the itch of the shorts he never got to make, but more about a hesitancy to step away completely from the iterative process by which he learned his craft — justifying the brief time he took off to make “Mama Bear” because he felt the need to sketch.

“It’s fun to have that playground because the features are bigger stakes,” said Barker. “We were like, ‘Okay, this is a short film: We can do weird stuff. Let’s come up with crazy rules that don’t make sense, and experiment.’”.

Barker and his “Mama Bear” cinematographer — his young brother Riley, who worked on the “Obsession” camera department — created different rules for the camera, as Curry is still trying to hone his discipline for storytelling within longer takes. Not only would they shoot a narrow 4:3 aspect ratio, but the Barker brothers denied themselves the ability to move the camera left, right, up, down, or dolly in.

“I do have a lot to learn,” noted Barker of making “Mama Bear.” “It’s so funny because I was having dinner and I told someone, ‘Oh, I’d love to shadow on Ari Aster’s set.’ And someone was like, ‘Well, you’re Curry Barker, what are you going to shadow for?’”.

His 2026 meteoric rise has allowed Barker to collect a group of more experienced peers he views as mentors — including Aster, Bill Hader, Zach Cregger, and Rian Johnson — and successful producers, like Jason Blum, investing in his career, but he believes there’s a misconception of what comes along with “making it.”.

“People think that once you’re in this club, you’re in the club, and everyone talks to everyone. But no — you’re in a bubble, and I want to know how Zach Cregger writes his outline. I want to watch him do it,” remarked Barker. “You’re all alone. Your process is your own, and you figure this stuff out on your own. Once you get into this league, there’s no one telling you, ‘Well, actually you do it like this, this, and this.’ It’s whatever you learned all along your journey; that’s your process.”.

One of the most impressive things about the self-taught Barker’s journey is how promptly he turned himself into a successful actor/writer/director/editor. In 2018, when Barker left Alabama to come to Los Angeles to pursue a career in movies, he saw himself as an actor. Despite all the story scenarios dancing around his head, the idea that he would become a screenwriter was laughable.

It has been revealed that “I never would’ve thought I was a screenwriter. I didn’t make great grades. I made Cs and Ds, and I wasn’t the best in English class,” said Barker, who naively assumed professional writers were the kids who won spelling bees: “I just thought to be respected as a writer you have to be that.” Barker credits taking screenwriter Aaron Sorkin’s MasterClass as what opened his eyes. “It was the first time I thought, ‘I can do this, too.’ It’s really just about being creative and cracking a story, and there are rules, there’s structure.”.

Sources indicate that directing organically grew out of Barker pulling together collaborators to shoot sketches and shorts for him to act in. Barker, half-joking, likes to say he realized one day that what he was doing was directing, and that he both enjoyed “telling people what to do” and had a knack for it.

What Barker accomplishes in a single shot — establishing a tonal balance that teeters between horror and comedy, combining blocking and camera movement to edit within the frame — is remarkably sophisticated. But Barker, who studies and strives for what masters like Kiyoshi Kurosawa can accomplish, quickly says he fell short in “Obsession.”.

“Things that you might think we pulled off [with longer takes in ‘Obsession’], we reshot,” remarked Barker, who on the podcast described in detail a key early scene between Bear (Michael Johnston) and Nikki (Inde Navarrette) in the bedroom that had to be reshot because the action took too long to unfold. “I think Ari [Aster] said once that if you realize you needed to give this information in four seconds, but then it took 25 seconds, you’re stuck with 25 seconds.”.

Curry Barker, the editor, is Curry Barker, the director’s harshest critic, giving him a bird’s-eye view of what he believes is the director’s inability to envision the required pacing of how a scene will play on screen, even if it might feel unnaturally fast on set.

According to recent reports, “Every single oner that I’ve shot in my career has been a problem in the edit,” mentioned Barker. “I think there’s two ways to fail at something. You can either fail, realize that it didn’t work, get scared of it, and then be like, ‘Well, in my last film I did a bunch of oners and then it killed me in the edit, so I’m not going to do that anymore.’ Or you can fail, realize how you did it wrong, and try to get better at that for the next time.”.

As Barker discussed at the Future of Filmmaking Summit last month, that iterative process is key to how he got where he is, and it’s a mindset he clearly hasn’t given up. When asked how “Obsession” would have been different if he had more money, Barker doesn’t talk about locations, sets, special or visual effects, or scenes he envisioned that he couldn’t pull off — in terms of scale, he likes both writing and directing within set limitations.

It has been revealed that “I would’ve reshot everything,” Barker answered without hesitation. “If I was finishing the edit before we got into TIFF, and you were like, ‘Dude, this is really good, we really love this movie, we think it has potential, but we want to give you $10 million to reshoot the whole thing, I would be like, ‘Deal.’ I would take it.”.

“I think it’s so funny to look back and think about that now,” Barker catches himself, knowing he’s talking about a film that broke the box office and catapulted his career. “Now I wouldn’t change anything because I would be too scared to touch it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of Survivor.

In a recent development, I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and I've been watching Survivor since day 1. The Open Era is officially upon us, meaning every single episode brings us at least one massive twist. Survivor 51 was been and entertaining ride on CBS (and streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) although there's been some backlash about problems related to the coin flip. I think I've got a solution for next season so that the episode's runtime doesn't spoil whether or not the flip is successful.

Industry observers note that mrBeast introduced the coin flip in Season 50, changing how much money Survivor contestants make. Last season Rick Devens successfully called it a doubled the prize pot, but poor Lewis Kelly was eliminated after his attempt this season. Unfortunately this scene wasn't all that thrilling to watch, as anyone who was watching live knew that there wasn't enough time in the episode for the contestants to vote and for host Jeff Probst to read them out. So what's the solution here?

Industry observers note that I think the way that we mitigate this moving forward and ensure that fans don't know the outcome of the coin flip is by having everyone vote BEFORE the flip. That way if the coin flip is indeed successful, Jeff can go right into revealing the votes. Hopefully this makes the runtime of the episode less of a spoiler in the process.

You might be thinking, but what if the person who successfully flips the coin was the target of the votes? This is definitely a possibility, but I think their immunity would work the same as if they had used a Hidden Immunity Idol. Those votes won't count, and the person with the second-most votes would be the one who gets eliminated from the game. Sure, the Survivor contestants will have to commit to their vote before finding out if the coin flip was successful, but I think that only adds a unique strategic challenge to the situation.

I'm just throwing out some options here, but it seems like the Survivor coin flip is here to stay. While the idea of the grand prize going up by million is thrilling, seeing Lewis lose was a real bummer, especially because he initially called it correctly in unseen footage. Anyone with a watch could see that he was going to end up going home, so I think that the producers need to find a way to keep the coin toss exciting. Hey, I'm happy to give them my idea with no strings attached.

According to recent reports, latest episodes of Survivor air Wednesdays on CBS as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Season 51 has been a wild ride so far, and I can only imagine the fireworks that are coming as we get deeper into the game.

For 15 seasons on Criminal Minds, Matthew Gray Gubler won over audiences as Dr. Spencer Reid, the endearing and hyper-intelligent FBI profiler. There's no doubt that while Reid was a genius and helped to solve cases because of his encyclopedic knowledge, he warmed hearts with his heartfelt and earnest nature. It was disappointing to see him not return to Criminal Minds: Evolution, but he'll soon be back on screens in another fun role.

It has been revealed that out of all the characters on the 15-year run of Criminal Minds, Reid proved that it took more than brawn to get a job done, even when in the field. He didn't even necessarily like to carry or use a gun, instead using his brains to catch killers and lure them into plots. There was even a chance to see the weight of being a genius, as it came with awkward social skills and the inability to sometimes get a joke. He was certainly missed when Criminal Minds returned with its Paramount+ revival, Evolution, with the show missing his quick ability to correct someone's facts and find a flaw in a pattern.

Recent findings suggest that the good news is it won't be long until Gubler is back on TV. CBS has released its midseason schedule, and Gubler's latest show Einstein is ready to rule CBS on Friday nights.

According to recent reports, while Reid's character has always been a genius and certainly had some fun moments, Gubler gets to show off more of his high-paced energy on Einstein. Lewis has often been described as a rebellious descendant of Albert Einstein, and that rebellious nature naturally leads to the character being a more fun version of Reid.

The best thing will be getting to see Gubler take on a character with a little more quirk. After serious storytelling on Criminal Minds, Gubler gets to lean into his comedic skills, and for those who have missed Gubler's signature quirky brilliance, his return to network TV is set to entertain.

In a recent development, lewis is likely to be more like Kaitlin Olson's Morgan on High Potential rather than Gubler's previous character, especially as he's teamed up with a more straight-laced cop in the form of Brooklyn Nine-Nine's Melissa Fumero's Teri. This level of genius can lead to the mind coming up with multiple theories at once. It's hard to focus on one particular problem, as there are so many other situations going on at the same time.

Industry observers note that add to the fact that he has a rebellious streak that leads to reckless behavior, there's a chance to show him choosing to get into trouble, even creating problems because he's bored or wants to get out of the situation he's put himself in. He's only working with the cops because it helps him avoid jail time, showing he's all for bending (and breaking) the rules.

In a recent development, with Gubler paired with Monk's Tony Shalhoub, who will play his father, there are plenty of opportunities for wild personal storylines. Not only has Shalhoub taken on a similar role on Monk, but he continued the fun as Midge's father on The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel. He has always brought passion and fast-paced commentary on a situation, allowing the two men to go back and forth in a battle of wits.

It has been revealed that while it's exciting to see Gubler back on the screen — and even in the lead — on broadcast TV, with Criminal Minds: Evolution coming to an end with its upcoming season, there are wishes to see him return as Spencer Reid. This is a little tricky due to production schedules, and there's also the fact that when Criminal Minds was filming, it wasn't set as the final season. It was only after production ended that Paramount+ decided to bring the show to an end, meaning that it wasn't set in a way to bring the goodbyes that the original Criminal Minds series on CBS could.

Industry observers note that einstein was in production between February and August 2026, while Criminal Minds: Evolution filmed until fall 2026. If the season finale was planned as a series finale, there could have been time to bring Reid back in a beautiful and meaningful goodbye moment, but it's highly unlikely.

In a recent development, bringing him back while Einstein was filming would have been near impossible due to how hectic the filming of a broadcast show is. There would have also needed to be a meaningful story to have him return, such as when he came back to be there for JJ after Will's death on Criminal Minds. Einstein premieres on February 12, 2027, giving us a fun and wild version of Reid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after landing his breakthrough Hollywood role as the blood-weeping baddie Le Chiffre in "Casino Royale," it seemed like Mads Mikkelsen would be a go-to villain for years to come. He was horrifyingly seductive as Dr. Hannibal Lecter in the NBC series "Hannibal," at which point it was hard to see mainstream viewers accepting him as anything other than a straight-up monster.

I don't know that he's turned the corner with American audiences, but there's ample evidence out there for moviegoers willing to go off the beaten path that Mikkelsen is terrifically effective as a hero. He can even be downright lovable, as he is in Thomas Vinterberg's booze-drenched comedy "Another Round" (where he gets to show off his hoofing chops).

According to recent reports, mikkelsen is not anywhere close to loveable in Kristian Levring's 2014 Western "The Salvation," but he is brutally compelling as a Danish combat veteran who settles east of the Mississippi River in the 1860s, and goes to war with a malevolent crime boss played with vicious glee by Jeffrey Dean Morgan. It's a different kind of role for Mikkelsen, and a departure for his "Casino Royale" co-star Eva Green as well. Whereas she was glamorous and wounded as Vesper Lynd, she's just flat-out wounded as Morgan's serially abused sister-in-law.

Industry observers note that levring conjures the widescreen majesty of Sergio Leone (replete with an Ennio Morricone-esque score), and depicts the violence with a matter-of-fact bluntness. Alas, despite receiving mostly good reviews (it holds a 72% Fresh rating at Rotten Tomatoes), it got unceremoniously dumped into U.S. theaters in 2015. It's presently available to stream on multiple services, so now is the time to catch up with it!

In a recent development, mikkelsen stars as Jon, who leaves Denmark with his brother Peter (Mikael Persbrandt) to start anew in America. Eventually, Jon's wife (Nanna Øland Fabricius) and son (Toke Lars Bjarke) join him, and the trio sets out on a stagecoach to begin the American chapter of their lives. Their hopes and dreams are immediately shattered when two criminals eject Jon from the stagecoach. The rape and kill his wife, and also murder his son.

According to recent reports, jon tracks down the coach, and kills the two men. That's revenge served piping hot, but it causes new troubles for Jon, as one of the murderers was the brother of ruthless gang leader Henry Delarue (Morgan). Delarue flies into a rage and begins killing townspeople, hoping to intimidate them into helping him capture Jon. Delarue's savagery knows no bounds, and he's especially fond of inflicting his cruelty on Green's mute Madelaine.

Industry observers note that levring isn't out to reinvent the genre. He just wants to make a good-and-bloody Western where the truly nasty bad guys get theirs before the credits roll. If you're a fan of the genre, this is a solid programmer filled with superb performances. So saddle up and get your gunslinging fix. (And then catch up with one of Mikkelsen's finest performances in "The Hunt").

Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps.
  • Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable consumers to generate nonconsensual nude images.
  • According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable consumers to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed consumers to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

It has been revealed that A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta noted they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same problems.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, mentioned that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

According to recent reports, revision, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple mentioned:.

Recent findings suggest that “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The company added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the manufacturer noted does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

In a recent development, as for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

It has been revealed that apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Revision, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

Sources indicate that apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps crucial issues and leaves out key context. The manufacturer says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The firm defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also notes it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out new child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the novel sold millions of copies, which meant a film adaptation was inevitable.
  • Recent findings suggest that "The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" (a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nicholas Evans' "The Horse Whisperer" was a publishing phenomenon in 1995. The novel is about a young girl who's involved in a horseback riding accident that kills her best friend and their horse, leaving her and her own horse seriously injured. When she falls into a deep funk, her mother whisks her off to rural Montana. There, they try to heal her horse emotionally via a horse whisperer. And while she is married, the mother finds herself falling in love with the handsome, deeply sensitive animal shrink, something which, according to many critics, transformed the narrative into a shamelessly sentimental romance à la "The Bridges of Madison County.".

In a recent development, the novel sold millions of copies, which meant a film adaptation was inevitable. Like "The Bridges of Madison County," the pedigree didn't make it immediately attractive to A-list directors. But Robert Redford saw something more in the material and took it on as his first directorial effort since his brilliant 1994 drama "Quiz Show." For the first time in his filmmaking career, Redford took the lead in his own movie. He also assembled a sensationally talented cast that included Kristin Scott Thomas, Dianne Wiest, Sam Neill, Chris Cooper, and Cherry Jones. For the role of the young girl, he and the casting team of Ellen Chenoweth and Gretchen Rennell went with up-and-comer Scarlett Johansson, who gave a moving performance that wound up being her breakthrough role.

Recent findings suggest that "The Horse Whisperer" isn't quite on the level of the movie version of "The Bridges of Madison County" (a lovely film that Clint Eastwood saved from production limbo), but the screenplay credited to Eric Roth and Richard LaGravenese is nuanced in a way that maybe the novel isn't. And though it's not one of Redford's best movies, it's a strong piece of work that deserves more attention.

It has been revealed that "The Horse Whisperer" holds a 72% Fresh critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $187 million at the worldwide box office upon hitting theaters. That was a decent result for Touchstone Pictures, but it didn't come close to matching the runaway success of its source material.

Robert Redford rarely failed to strike up chemistry with his leading ladies ("The Great Gatsby" being a notable exception), so it's hardly a shocker that he's perfectly paired with Kristin Scott Thomas. This is not, however, a heated attraction, as Redford's character is still mourning the end of a previous romance where the woman chose the city over him and the country. Thomas is from the city, too (and, again, married), so he's worried that another heartbreak is around the corner.

Industry observers note that as for Scarlett Johansson, she captures the grief of a young woman whose life has been irreparably changed. Her leg was partially amputated, which she fears will make her undesirable to romantic partners as she gets older. This gives rise to the most overpoweringly emotional scene in the movie when, after a row with her mother, Johansson's character tearfully asks, "Who's going to want me?" If that doesn't switch on your waterworks, go straight to the doctor, because your heart isn't properly functioning.

Industry observers note that "The Horse Whisperer" is available to rent via streaming, but the film is badly in need of a digital restoration. Hopefully, Disney will commission one at some point, although I'm not sure if the movie is a popular enough library title to merit such treatment.

Industry News: How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, [Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival.
  • World-class Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (“Leviathan”) returned to the Croisette this year in Cannes competition with “Minotaur,” having recovered from a near-fatal illness.
  • It has been revealed that when he left the hospital in Germany in 2022, as he told me while at Cannes this year, he was in a wheelchair.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, [Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. MUBI will release “Minotaur” in theaters on Friday, November 20.].

World-class Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev (“Leviathan”) returned to the Croisette this year in Cannes competition with “Minotaur,” having recovered from a near-fatal illness. After contracting a severe case of COVID in 2021, he reacted badly to the Sputnik vaccine and was put into a medically induced coma for 14 days. When he came out of it, his arms and legs were paralyzed due to Guillain-Barré Syndrome. He lay flat on his back for a year.

It has been revealed that when he left the hospital in Germany in 2022, as he told me while at Cannes this year, he was in a wheelchair. While he states he hasn’t watched TV for 20 years now, “I watched a lot of films online,” he said through an interpreter on the roof of the Palais. “I read some things. I did not know if I would ever be able to walk again, to live again as a normal person. I have still now some consequences. I’m not at my best. I have regained completely the motion of my hands, but I have still a bit of a difficulty walking.” Related Stories Rian Johnson Leaves the Door Open to Star Wars Return: ‘It’s a World I Deeply Love’ Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Debuts to Mighty $120 Million, Reviving Lionsgate’s Most Important Franchise.

But he did manage to shoot his sixth feature film last year, but not in Russia. After nine months of waiting, in the spring of 2023, he let go of one expensive project (“Jupiter”) for which he couldn’t seem to raise funding. “I said, ‘Let’s put it on ice, we’ll come back to it later. I don’t want to sit and wait for years and years for you to find the money. I want to make a film now.'”.

So instead the filmmaker focused on a parallel project he had also been developing, an adaptation of Claude Chabrol’s 1969 thriller “The Unfaithful Wife,” starring Stéphane Audran as a well-heeled wife cheating on her husband, which was later remade as “Unfaithful” with Richard Gere and Diane Lane. The result, “Minotaur,” is the “Leviathan” Oscar nominee’s first film in nearly a decade, since 2017’s “Loveless.”.

At the same time that the filmmaker was coping with his illness, four years ago, at the start of the Ukraine war, he made the decision to leave Russia and move to Paris. Going home would mean the risk of being considered a traitor or an enemy of the state in Russia. “It might result in us becoming what is called foreign agents; it’s a hard thing,” he mentioned. “Maybe this will happen, maybe not. Let’s not be too pessimistic, but mostly all independent journalists are saying that their oppressions are going to get even harsher, and that I think we have decades ahead of us before things get better.”.

It has been revealed that his 16-year-old had been studying at a French high school in Moscow before the war. “His French was pretty good,” remarked Zvyagintsev. “So it was an obvious choice. And also, my wife [has been] in love with France for a long time, she has been learning French for many years. So it was a choice, also for both of them, and for their future.”.

How’s his French? “Zero,” he noted. “The other reason for me was that France is the homeland to cinema; that’s where cinema was born, and also there are so many cinephiles among spectators. Also here in France, directors have the final cut. In the states, it’s much harder to get in a position where you are not censored; it’s not a producer or someone who decides instead of you.”.

Recent findings suggest that the filmmaker set about creating believable Russian locations in Riga, Latvia, which still resembles its neighbor country. “The dormitory suburbs around Riga look exactly like Russian dormitory suburbs,” said Zvyagintsev. “A Russian eye would not be able to distinguish between Russia and Latvia in this instance. As for interiors, Anton’s flat was constructed as a set, so it’s a constructed set, and the villa where the main characters live is a contemporary building, a very modern one, and you could find something exactly like this anywhere.”.

When it came to finding his cast, the casting director put out a call for Russian characters of a certain age. “Every actor from anywhere who is interested in working with you, they will send you a video presentation,” mentioned Zvyagintsev. “They can be from Argentina, London, Moscow, Paris, wherever. You send them a scene they have to play, and they make a self-tape for you on their iPhone. Before, I despised self-tapes, but it’s convenient, because now with everybody scattered around the world, it’s the only way for us to work. We could not possibly pay for all the people I wanted to check to come to Riga to make a real-life casting. There were people also from Riga who do speak Russian.”.

Industry observers note that one serious glitch for Russian actors still living in Russia was the possible repercussions of participating in a Zvyagintsev project. “I would talk to them about the script and show them parts of the script, so that they know what they’re getting involved in, because, of course, they were at risk of getting blacklisted,” he mentioned. “Most of them, with heartache, refused to take part in the film, but there was one who accepted, and I’m still completely amazed at his courage. It’s the main part, the main character, [actor] Dmitriy Mazurov. I said to him, ‘Are you sure you want to film with me?’ And he said, ‘If I’m not doing this part, I don’t know what I’m doing in acting.'”.

According to recent reports, of course, the filmmaker took a different approach to the Chabrol story. “In the first minute, the story is completely revealed,” he said. “We understand that she is being unfaithful, so then all the film is about observing him, observing her, trying to understand, hesitating, and trying to guess what is going on, and while he observes, the spectator starts doing it along with him. And after the murder, actually, he goes back to this position where he’s mostly observing her reaction to the disappearance of a lover, yeah, and she knows what’s going on, and again it’s about observation.”.

Sources indicate that the filmmaker loved one bravura sequence that is 20 minutes long without any dialogue at all. “The sequence after the murder, it’s 20 minutes, even a little bit more, with not one subtitle, so you only observe his actions, and there are no words: it’s extremely cinematic in its essence.”.

And Zvyagintsev added many telling details from the real world, from corruption to the war. “The Chabrol film is much more classical,” he said. “It follows a pattern: he killed, then he’s discovered, and then he will be punished. And I wanted to break up this classical structure and to invent something different based on our Russian realities.”.

It has been revealed that was shooting the movie a physical challenge? “When you are full of inspiration, when you are searching constantly for solutions, the light, the sets, the performance of the actors, you don’t feel fatigued in the same way,” he said. “There is such a joy in making the film that is, in your head, real. I think it’s the best drug there is.”.

Next up, he will try and resuscitate “Jupiter.” ” I have met some producers who are interested in it,” he remarked, “so hopefully we will be able to get it moving again.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I spend a lot of time keeping up with the 2026 TV schedule, but Sunday afternoon I was at Arrowhead Stadium, sitting in Section 107, Row 27, watching Travis Kelce catch two touchdowns against the Arizona Cardinals in person. It was a pretty good day to be a Kansas City Chiefs fan. While I watched Patrick Mahomes and Kelce go to work on the field, a different conversation was brewing online about a familiar hand gesture from the tight end's wife, Taylor Swift. Sorry, Swifties, she wasn’t giving her "peace sign" while celebrating her Dear Husband’s touchdowns.

It has been revealed that in one clip, Swift held up two fingers, prompting some fans to wonder if she was flashing her familiar peace sign. Having been there for the game, I think I can help clear this one up. Those two fingers had a pretty straightforward explanation: her DH had just scored two touchdowns. The videos of her celebrating with the Kelce family are awfully cute and also clear up the situation.

🎥| Taylor with the most joyous touchdown celebration for her husband!😊 https://t.co/udtlrbvBA4November 22, 2026.

Industry observers note that now, I didn't have a view into the family suite from my seat. Still, I did watch a woman in front of me continuously use her phone to zoom in and scan the box for, I assume, Taylor. Unfortunately it was to no avail, if her body language was any indication. Thankfully, the broadcast cameras and fans with a clearer vantage point of Taylor dutifully had it covered.

Swift has had plenty of company at Chiefs games this season, including Caitlin Clark, who recently admitted they both got nervous while watching Kelce play. This time Swift watched with her parents, Scott and Andrea, as well as Donna Kelce, sister-in-law Kylie Kelce, and some of the Kelce kids. After Travis' second touchdown, the cameras caught one particularly adorable moment when Swift bent down to embrace Jason and Kylie's oldest daughter, Wyatt.

Industry observers note that wyatt, 7, looks absolutely delighted, and Swift is just as animated. There's something especially sweet about seeing them celebrate together, considering the little girl has gone from knowing her uncle's famous girlfriend as "Taylor Swift" to having her as Aunt Taylor after Swift and Kelce's July wedding. If I were Wyatt, I'd be telling that story at school for the rest of the year.

The moment was cute enough that fans kept sharing it, including another post celebrating it. The Kelce family has given viewers plenty of entertaining moments over the years, but watching a kid light up because her uncle scored a touchdown is hard to beat.

Sources indicate that some viewers understandably took the two-finger celebration as a peace sign, which isn't exactly an unreasonable assumption. We've already seen a simple gesture from Swift cause a stir when she pointed to her wedding ring after an earlier Kelce touchdown, so I understand why fans were paying attention. Except this time, those of us following the action on the field had an answer ready. Kelce scored twice, and his wife was keeping count. Besides, Kelce has talked about how much of a football expert Swift has become, so I have a feeling she knew exactly what she was celebrating.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Patrick Mahomes found Kelce for an 8-yard score on the Chiefs' opening possession. Then, late in the second quarter, the quarterback connected with him again on a 22-yard touchdown pass. Kelce finished with six catches for 74 yards as Kansas City beat Arizona 34-7.

Sources indicate that it was a pretty significant day for Kelce beyond giving his wife a reason to wave two fingers in the air. His first touchdown moved him past Rob Gronkowski for third place in career touchdowns among tight ends when postseason scores are included. He also hadn't caught two touchdowns in a regular-season game since 2022. That gives me one more reason to appreciate the game I happened to catch in person.

A postgame clip of Kelce even circulated after the win, because apparently fans weren't quite ready to call it a day on 'Tay and Trav Watch' even when the clock hit zero.

Sources indicate that the Chiefs have a quick turnaround before facing the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, which you can watch on NBC or stream live with a Peacock subscription. As for my Sunday at Arrowhead, I'll remember seeing Kelce score twice. Thanks to the viral videos, I'll also remember Swift celebrating with Wyatt. We can officially file that supposed peace sign under "two touchdowns.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's a lot to love in Grand Theft Auto 6, but many of those strengths were overshadowed by basic game features. Take, for instance, GTA 6's hated autosave feature. Normally, autosave is something that players don't have to worry much about as it happens entirely in the background. Yet GTA 6's implementation of this basic feature literally brought some players to tears.

Sources indicate that the issue was one of frequency. Previously, GTA 6 seemed to mostly autosave between missions, or at major mission checkpoints. This meant that players could sometimes make lots of progress on ambient world tasks, like sticking up a store or going shopping, only to lose it all after closing the game down improperly or reloading.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is overflowing with distractions from the main missions, though — you could theoretically play it for hours on end without actually getting further into the story. Unfortunately, this led to some high-profile cases in which streamers and average players alike lost half a dozen hours or more of progress​​​​​​​. In one particularly egregious case, Twitch streamer JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress and then was swatted​​​​​​​ shortly after the shocking discovery.

Sources indicate that fear no more, because Rockstar is on the case. One of the bullet points on the Nov. 23​​​​​​​ update reads, "Fixed an issue that resulted in the game not autosaving correctly." The update hasn't been out for long, so we can't verify exactly how GTA 6 addresses the issue. Given the nature of the complaints leading up to the update, though, it seems reasonable to assume that the game's autosave is not strictly tied to mission progress. Perhaps it even autosaves a little more often?​​​​​​​.

Whatever the case, it's nice to see that Rockstar has its fingers on the pulse of what players want most. Beyond some nuts-and-bolts fixes​​​​​​​, GTA 6's first major patch also ensures that the game's dynamic weather system actually works as intended. Previously, players had put many hours into the game without seeing so much as a thunderstorm.

The 01.002.002 enhancement is rolling out gradually for players on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, so if you don't see it yet, hang tight — and keep saving manually — and often​​​​​​​!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its owners’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let customers edit a Story after publishing.

This means owners will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”.

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:.

A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri).

Today’s revision is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

It has been revealed that back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting users manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

The original "Hunger Games" raised the stakes for Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) by establishing that tributes from their home, District 12, have only ever won the Hunger Games twice in 74 years. That means they only have one mentor, the alcoholic Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson), unlike other Districts' tributes that have two mentors each.

According to recent reports, "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins told the story of the first District 12 victor in "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" — Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), who won the 10th Hunger Games decades before Katniss was born and then vanished. Now, "Sunrise on the Reaping" tells how Haymitch won his own Hunger Games.

Haymitch was at a disadvantage before he even entered the arena, since there were no District 12 victors available to mentor him. To address this issue, the Capitol "borrowed" victors from other districts and assigned them to mention Haymitch and his fellow District 12 tributes. Those mentors are Mags Flanagan (Lili Taylor) and Wiress (Maya Hawke), younger versions of characters who first appeared in the second "Hunger Games" film/book, "Catching Fire.".

Wiress (played by Amanda Plummer back in "Catching Fire") isn't in the movie much, but "Hunger Games" fans will likely recognize the actress playing her. The daughter of Ethan Hawke and Uma Thurman, Maya Hawke is one of the more charming "nepo babies" to come out of recent Hollywood.

Hawke has been acting in film and television since 2017, when she played Jo March in a BBC production of "Little Women." In 2019, she not only appeared in Quentin Tarantino's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" as "Flower Child," a member of the Manson family; she also got her massive break. Hawkey joined "Stranger Things" in its third season as Robin Buckley, working alongside Steve Harrington (Joe Keery) at mall ice cream store Scoops Ahoy.

Recent findings suggest that the season seems to set up Robin and Steve as a latest romantic couple ... until she reveals she's not into guys! Despite the show taking place in the 1980s, though, Steve is cool with it. While Season 3 of "Stranger Things" tends to be remembered as one of its weaker outings, Robin was a great addition to the ensemble and Hawke returned as part of the main cast for the subsequent two seasons.

In a recent development, hawke has also worked alongside her father. In historical miniseries "The Good Lord Bird," where Ethan Hawke starred as radical abolitionist John Brown, Maya Hawke played Brown's daughter, Annie. When Ethan Hawke directed the Flannery O'Connor biopic "Wildcat" in 2023, he cast Maya as the famed author.

It has been revealed that maya Hawke's other film roles include parts in Wes Anderson's "Asteroid City," Pixar sequel "Inside Out 2" as the voice of Anxiety, and a part in the upcoming "Magic: The Gathering" film. Hawke is also a singer-songwriter and has released four studio albums ("Blush," "Moss," "Chaos Angel," and "Maitreya Corso") as of 2026.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is now in theaters.

Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch.
  • Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
  • Sources indicate that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”.

Sources indicate that when they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she notes.

Dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He claims to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”.

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting fresh additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

Industry observers note that in Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a major blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy demonstrated me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”.

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” says Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”.

Sources indicate that villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”.

It has been revealed that when Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she claims. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the significant surprises in the ensemble.”.

According to recent reports, taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” notes Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”.

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” indicates Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”.

It has been revealed that pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”.

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” claims Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she states. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most key for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last week, huge news broke that Robert Pattinson would be playing James Bond in the upcoming, as-yet-untitled 26th Bond film. Immediately, all kinds of memes started popping up everywhere and that is, at least in some part, because Pattinson is, of course, very famous. He is arguably the biggest star ever cast as Bond, though Pierce Brosnan was pretty famous when he got the gig in the early ‘90s.

A lot of Bond fans, myself included, were surprised, despite the rumors, that Amazon MGM went with an established star. Jeff Bezos recently spoke about the decision and addressed this very matter and highlighted how they didn’t think he’d end up in the role.

According to recent reports, while speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World last week, the Amazon boss was asked about the casting, and like many of us, he explained that initially they thought they would go with more of an unknown–or least someone less known–than an actor who has already been part of three monster franchises The Batman, Twilight, and Dune. During Bezos’ chat at the conference, he remarked:.

Sources indicate that initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.

Bezos also talked about how involved the process was once the creators nailed down their final choices, reportedly: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, and Pattinson. It wasn’t a simple audition process, as Bezos explained:.

It has been revealed that I was heavily involved. We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a massive group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. It was really interesting: full costume, real sets, other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists.

In the end, much to my relief, it sounds like everyone involved was on the same page. Bezos praised all the actors who screen-tested, but Pattinson clearly stood out among the five finalists. Noted Bezos:.

Sources indicate that all the actors were extraordinarily talented. By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances, and it was kind of immediately ‘undebated.’ Denis [Villeneuve], the director, was… we all sort of gravitated to him.

In a recent development, opinions on Pattinson becoming the ninth man to play James Bond have varied greatly, as to be expected. Many online were cheering the decision, while many others were unhappy with the choice. As a huge Bond fan (and someone who often uses his Prime subscription to rewatch the movies), I’m good with it. I want to see him play 007 before I form an opinion, as I think everyone should. Clearly, he was the first choice among the producers and, at least for now, we should trust them. Now...about that latest Bond girl.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “Disclosure Day,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences.

One of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories Rian Johnson Leaves the Door Open to Star Wars Return: ‘It’s a World I Deeply Love’ Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Debuts to Mighty $120 Million, Reviving Lionsgate’s Most Key Franchise.

Industry observers note that “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler noted. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.”.

Recent findings suggest that but while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic.

Industry observers note that “When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.”.

More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks.

Dustin Hoffman's Forgotten HBO Drama Series Was Canceled For A Tragic Reason

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, HBO launched on November 8, 1972, and has since produced some of the finest highlights in television history.
  • Recent findings suggest that david Milch began his career on "Hill Street Blues" before co-creating one of the best reveals of the 1990s in "NYPD Blue." That alone would be enough to make him a TV legend, but Milch wasn't done.
  • Recent findings suggest that his 2006 series, "John from Cincinnati," was a strange affair that lasted just one season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, HBO launched on November 8, 1972, and has since produced some of the finest highlights in television history. It has also produced plenty of swiftly forgotten and overlooked curios, many of which are actually quite good. The Dustin Hoffman-led "Luck" was, according to critics at least, one example. This horse racing drama looked set to be another ongoing hit for the network until it was canceled following the deaths of three horses involved in production, bringing a tragic end to the show despite the fact it had already been renewed.

Recent findings suggest that david Milch began his career on "Hill Street Blues" before co-creating one of the best reveals of the 1990s in "NYPD Blue." That alone would be enough to make him a TV legend, but Milch wasn't done. He managed to steer clear of the ill-advised "NYPD Blue" spin-off "Public Morals," which was canceled after one episode, but he did oversee his share of short-lived crime series in "Brooklyn South," "Total Security," and "Big Apple." It wasn't until 2004 that he struck gold again with the HBO series "Deadwood," arguably the best Western TV show ever made. After that, however, Milch's career involved creating little-known series that came and went without making much of an impact.

Recent findings suggest that his 2006 series, "John from Cincinnati," was a strange affair that lasted just one season. "Luck," on the other hand, looked as though it could break the trend and go the distance. Set in the world of horse racing, the Hoffman-fronted series also benefited from the directorial talents of none other than Michael Mann, and became a critical hit, earning a second season renewal. But that second season never materialized after some unfortunate on-set events which forced HBO to cancel "Luck" despite the fact filming had already started on Season 2.

"Luck" was somewhat of a passion project for David Milch, who told the Los Angeles Times, "I've been thinking about doing a show like this for 25 years." The creator explained how his father had taken him to horse racing events since he was age five or six, and how he saw the horses as "heart-stopping beautiful." All of which just makes the story of "Luck" even more tragic.

Dustin Hoffman plays Chester "Ace" Bernstein, a gambler who after coming home after a three-year stay in federal prison immediately concocts a initiative for revenge against those who helped put him away. His bodyguard, driver, and right hand man, Gus (Dennis Farina) acts as front for Ace's investment in race horse Pint of Plain. Meanwhile, Hoffman's gambler sets out to restore the failing Santa Anita racetrack as part of his plan for retribution. Nick Nolte also appears as a veteran trainer who now owns his own colt.

"Luck" premiered in January 2012 to positive reviews and looked as though it might have the potential to become one of the best HBO reveals of all time. By the end of that month, the show had already earned a second season renewal. On January 31, 2012, the Los Angeles Times reported that HBO had ordered a further 10 episodes that were set to debut in January 2013, with production on the new season set to get underway in February. According to the outlet, the debut episode brought in 1.1 million viewers and the renewal was "hardly shocking" given Hoffman and Nolte's involvement. What was shocking, however, was that on March 14, 2012, the Los Angeles Times once again reported on the show, this time to announce it had been canceled altogether.

"Luck" Season 1 earned an 82% certified fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with critics praising the cast and writing in particular. But behind all this success, there was trouble brewing. People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) had been on top of HBO and "Luck" since January 2012, the month in which the show debuted. According to The Hollywood Reporter, the organization had written to the channel to enquire as to the treatment of horses used in the show, and had followed up on numerous occasions thereafter.

Industry observers note that as a report from PETA explains, two horses were euthanized during production of the first season. According to the group, "older, arthritic horses had been used in dangerous (and deadly) racing sequences" leading to the two euthanizations. What's more, the report cites "insiders at Santa Anita Race Track" as having provided information about a third horse that died on-set. Rather than push on, HBO pulled the plug and "Luck" was added to the expansive list of the best demonstrates canceled after only one season.

A statement from HBO (via the LA Times), read, "It is with heartbreak that executive producers David Milch and Michael Mann together with HBO have decided to cease all future production on the series 'Luck.'" The network claimed to have maintained "the highest safety standards throughout production," but acknowledged that "accidents unfortunately happen and it is impossible to guarantee they won't in the future." "Luck" Season 1 continued to air, but production on Season 2 was brought to an end despite plenty of footage having already been shot. Today, Season 1 remains available on HBO Max.

💡 Key Takeaways
